neighbours.label: Youth subcultures and alternative music or lifestyle scenes (punk, grunge, acid jazz, skateboarding, hip-hop and graffiti, pot-smoking hippies), firing on the scene's name; mainstream or establishment pastimes in the same frames stay quiet.
fire: As a teenager he lived for hardcore punk shows and skate parks.
The band mixed surf rock with garage psych and a bit of grunge.
She spent the nineties in the goth scene, dyeing her hair black.
Their zine covered acid jazz, trip-hop and underground raves.
The kids on our block were into breakdancing and graffiti.
My uncle was a stoner who followed the Grateful Dead around the country.
In art school he discovered emo music and skateboarding.
The festival drew hippies, bikers and heavy metal fans.
quiet: As a teenager he lived for chess tournaments and the debate club.
The orchestra mixed Brahms with Mozart and a bit of Haydn.
She spent the nineties in the church choir, singing every Sunday.
Their newsletter covered opera, ballet and chamber concerts.
The kids on our block were into baseball and swimming.
My uncle was a banker who followed the stock market every day.
In art school he discovered oil painting and pottery.
The festival drew families, gardeners and flower show fans.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks on ' jazz' (acid jazz), ' жизнь' (sex life), ' Pie' (American Pie), ' on' (smokes marijuana on), ' meme' (kink meme), 'vana' (Nirvana).
